subject: Pilot spend gating — monthly band validation & PO trigger options
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@fintegrate.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot spend gating — monthly band validation & PO trigger options

Hi Elena / Carlos — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps on the budget side so procurement has what it needs to move forward.

Key points from our call:
- Primary pilot: 3 internal apps (search, chat assistant, content gen) with mixed sync/async traffic.
- Expected steady state token mix: ~80% generation, 20% embeddings/rerank.
- Rough throughput: 40–100M tokens/month during pilot depending on daily cadence.
- Target unit: we discussed a target price in the neighborhood of $20–$40 / 1M tokens for the pilot commitment window.

What I attached: Fintegrate_Monthly_Band_Range.xlsx — a simple sensitivity table mapping token bands to monthly spend and recommended PO trigger thresholds. Also attached a first-pass SOW for the pilot (SOW_Draft_v1.pdf).

Recommended procurement framing (proposal):
1) Pilot monthly band: $2k–$4k / month (low) | $8k–$12k / month (expected) | $20k+ / month (high) — these map to ~40M / 100M / 300M tokens at the target unit economics.
2) PO trigger tiers: no PO for < $5k/mo; single-month PO for $5k–$15k; committed PO (60/90 day) for $15k+ to shorten lead times.
3) Escrow / prepay option: we can support a prepaid credit balance to give you predictable unit pricing with admin simplicity.

Open asks for you / procurement:
- Can you confirm whether Fintegrate will require a formal PO for pilot costs under $10k/month?
- Who in procurement owns PO thresholds and vendor onboarding (name + email)?
- Do you have a preferred billing cadence (monthly vs. net-30 with PO)?

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm procurement's PO threshold and owner (EOD Thu 5/13 if possible).
- We update the SOW to include the escrow/prepay option and a sample PO clause.
- If acceptable, we can provision a 60-day pilot with an initial credit and metric-based rollover.

Thanks — I’ll hold off on contract edits until procurement confirms the PO threshold.

Best,
Ava

--
Ava Chen

From: Elena Morales <elena@fintegrate.com>

Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot spend gating — monthly band validation & PO trigger options

Thanks Ava — great summary. A few clarifications from procurement side:

- We typically require a PO for any recurring spend that exceeds $7,500 per month; below that we can use our vendor card or a one-off invoice.
- Procurement owner for vendor setup is Maria Gonzalez (m.gonzalez@fintegrate.com) — she’ll handle vendor docs and onboarding.
- Billing cadence preference: monthly invoices with net-30 is standard for us; prepaid is possible but needs approval from finance for the pilot.

On token bands: your high case aligns with internal estimates. If we can keep the unit price at ~$25 / 1M tokens for the expected band (~100M/month), that would fit our forecast.

I’ll loop Maria in once we have a mocked-up SOW that includes payment options.

Elena

--
Elena Morales
Head of Product | Fintegrate
elena@fintegrate.com
From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@fintegrate.com>, Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@fintegrate.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 08:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot spend gating — monthly band validation & PO trigger options

Thanks for the quick details, Elena — super helpful. Copying Karthik so he can incorporate Fintegrate's PO floor and billing cadence into the SOW.

Proposal update (per your notes):
- We’ll mark the PO threshold at $7.5k/mo in the SOW. Pilot pricing options we’ll show:
  a) Pay-as-you-go monthly invoices (net-30) — baseline pricing.
  b) Prepaid credit balance — 5% discount on unit price for pilot if prepaid upfront.
  c) Committed short-term commitment (60 days) — reduce unit price further (we can model this once you confirm expected tokens).

Karthik — please take the attached workbook and produce two rows we can present to Maria: (1) Expected band (~100M tokens/mo) at a $25 / 1M token rate, net-30 monthly invoice; (2) Prepay 100% of 2-months at a 5% discount, show resulting $/1M token and total invoice amount. Also add a sample PO clause that says: "PO required for recurring monthly spend >= $7,500; Redwood invoices monthly net-30 unless a prepaid credit balance is in place."

Elena — if Maria needs a vendor form or W9, we can get that to you within 24 hours. If you want, we can include an escrow-style prepay option language that allows unused credits to roll over for 90 days.

Action items:
- Elena: confirm Maria contact and whether finance will consider prepay for pilot (EOD Thu).
- Karthik: send two-row cost table + sample PO clause (EOD Wed).

Thanks — talk soon.

Ava
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot spend gating — monthly band validation & PO trigger options

Quick internal note for the thread (we’ll send polished output to Elena/Maria):

- I produced the two scenarios Ava requested and attached a small summary (copied into the SOW). Key numbers:
  • Scenario A (monthly invoice, net-30): 100M tokens/mo at $25 / 1M => $2,500 / month. (Note: that's lower than their stated expected $8k–$12k bracket — they may be counting tokens differently; double-check generation vs embedding splits and tokenization assumptions.)
  • Scenario B (2-month prepay, 5% discount): Effective unit = $23.75 / 1M => 100M tokens * 2 months = 200M tokens => Invoice ~ $4,750 prepay.

- Recommend we: (1) call out in the SOW sample an explicit token definition and include a short prompt/response example so procurement understands how tokens map to spend; (2) include the PO clause as Ava suggested with the $7.5k threshold; (3) surface an option for a 60-day capped commitment if they want predictable runway above $15k/mo.

I’ll drop the two-row table into the shared drive link and send to Maria once Ava gives the go-ahead.

Karthik
